title: Quinoa vs. Bulgur: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Quinoa vs. Bulgur: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Cooked bulgur usually has more fiber and fewer calories; quinoa has slightly more protein and is naturally gluten-free. Compare per 100 g cooked.
seo.search_intent: Compare quinoa and bulgur for protein, fiber, calories, gluten, and minerals.

excerpt: Per 100 g cooked, quinoa provides about 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber; bulgur about 83 calories, 3.1 g protein, and 4.5 g fiber. Bulgur is whole wheat and contains gluten, while quinoa is naturally gluten-free.
content_html:
Quinoa and bulgur are both popular alternatives to rice, but their strongest nutritional features differ. Bulgur leads on fiber and calorie density; quinoa has a small protein advantage and is naturally gluten-free.

Per 100 g cooked

Cooked quinoa is roughly 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber. Cooked bulgur is about 83 calories, 3.1 g protein, and 4.5 g fiber.

So the idea that quinoa is always the higher-fiber choice is wrong: bulgur often has substantially more fiber per cooked weight.

Why bulgur counts as a whole grain

Bulgur is made from whole wheat that has been parboiled, dried, and cracked. It retains the bran, germ, and endosperm in whole-grain proportions.

Gluten

Bulgur contains gluten because it is wheat. Quinoa does not naturally contain gluten.

Which one should you choose?

For maximum fiber with relatively few calories, bulgur is excellent if gluten is not an issue. For gluten-free eating or a different amino-acid profile, quinoa has the advantage.

Neither wins every category; the better choice depends on what you want from the meal.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Cooked bulgur usually has more: around 4.5 g/100 g versus roughly 2.8 g/100 g for quinoa.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Quinoa usually has a modest edge: about 4.4 g/100 g versus 3.1 g/100 g.

faq.question: Does bulgur contain gluten?
faq.answer: Yes. Bulgur is made from wheat.
